title: The Disc Miner. II. Revealing gas substructures and kinematic signatures from planet-disc interaction through line profile analysis
question: Identify potential signatures from planet-disc interaction and gas substructures in the circumstellar discs around MWC 480, HD 163296, AS 209, IM Lup, and GM Aur through line profile analysis of CO isotopologues.

what.value: JvM-corrected images with robust=0.5 from the MAPS survey

evidence.loc: Observations and models
evidence.quote: We use the JvM-corrected images with a robust parameter of 0.5 (cite: czekala+2021)

evidence.loc: Extended velocity and line width perturbations
evidence.quote: For this experiment, we fix the $^{12}$CO model surface to the non-parametric emitting layer extracted by (cite: paneque+2022), and re-run DISCMINER to find a new set of parameters for the remaining attributes summarised in Table 1.

what.value: Millimetre continuum disc inclination for MWC 480

evidence.loc: Extended velocity and line width perturbations
evidence.quote: For better comparison, we also fix the disc inclination in both the smooth and irregular-surface model to the value found by (cite: liu+2019) from mm continuum modelling.

recipe.goal: Model channel-by-channel molecular line intensity cubes
recipe.method: Fit parametric 3D channel-map models to the observed data cubes using a generalised bell function line profile kernel for upper and lower emission surfaces
key_parameters: Orientation (i, PA, x_c, y_c), Velocity (M_*, v_sys), Upper and Lower surface (z_0, p, R_t, q), Peak intensity (I_0, p, q), Line width (L_w0, p, q), Line slope (L_s0, p); normalisation D_0=100 au
For AS 209 12CO, asymmetric intensity normalisation: 0.65 I_0 for -80 deg < phi < 80 deg, and 1.25 I_0 otherwise
assumptions: Keplerian rotation with vertical differential rotation sustained by balance of forces in the z-direction
Highest intensity between upper and lower surface components taken on each pixel and velocity channel
Axisymmetric intensity fields for all model channels except 12CO of AS 209

recipe.goal: Extract line profile observables and compute deprojected residual maps
recipe.method: Fit Gaussian kernels to both data and model line profiles to extract peak intensity, line width, and centroid velocity; subtract model from data and deproject onto the disc reference frame using retrieved vertical structure and orientation
key_parameters: Peak intensity, line width, and centroid velocity

recipe.goal: Detect localised velocity and line width perturbations via clustering
recipe.method: Fold residual maps across the disc minor axis, divide disc radial extent into annuli, extract peak residuals per annulus, group peak residuals into radial and azimuthal clusters using K-means, and identify significant clusters
key_parameters: Annulus width = 1/4 of the beam size; significance threshold = 3 sigma of spectral variance of peak residuals

recipe.goal: Decompose velocity residuals into azimuthal and vertical (meridional) velocity components and radial profiles
recipe.method: Compute azimuthal averages (over 2pi or symmetric section psi) of standard velocity residuals to obtain vertical velocity v_z, and of absolute velocity residuals to obtain azimuthal velocity perturbation Delta v_phi, alongside azimuthally averaged radial profiles of peak intensity and line width residuals
key_parameters: Standard residuals (v_0,d - v_0,m) and absolute residuals (|v_0,d - v_sys,m| - |v_0,m - v_sys,m|)
assumptions: Three-dimensional components of the velocity field are axisymmetric and line-of-sight velocities are dominated by azimuthal velocities

answer_key.quantity: MWC 480 planet candidate orbital radius

evidence.loc: Abstract
evidence.quote: In MWC 480, we identified non-axisymmetric line width enhancements around the radial separation of candidate planet-driven buoyancy spirals, which we used to narrow the location of the possible planet to an orbital radius of $R=245$ au and $\rm{PA}=193^\circ$, at a projected distance of $1.33"$ from the star.

evidence.loc: Extended velocity and line width perturbations
evidence.quote: Considering this and the fact that the vertical velocity signatures are in good agreement with those expected for a planet-driven buoyancy spiral, we propose a planet candidate in the disc of MWC 480 at an orbital radius of $R=245$ au, namely at the radial location proposed by (cite: teague+2021), but at an azimuth of $\phi=-128^\circ$, where the peak in $^{12}$CO line width residuals is found.
